---
name: check-in-flight-work-before-claiming
description: "./hq board misses cloud-agent work Ellis dispatched without a claim; check PRs, branches, worktrees and Entire trails before picking issues"
metadata:

---

On 2026-11-14 I picked #44 and #52 from `./hq board` (it showed 0 in progress), but Ellis already had Conductor and Cursor cloud workspaces building #112, #43, #52, #44 and #35. None of them had claimed, so the board looked free. Ellis stopped me and I had to release my #44 claim.

**Why:** cloud agents skip `./hq claim`, so their issues stay `status:ready` until a PR appears. A claim on top of them blocks their own `./hq` steps.

**How to apply:** before picking, check every signal and treat any lane with in-flight work as taken:
- `./hq board`: labels and claims;
- `gh pr list`: open PRs, especially `cursor/*` branches;
- `git branch -r`: remote branches;
- `git worktree list`: Conductor workspaces and agent worktrees;
- `entire trail list --project gh/ehewes`: a trail in the "building" phase is work in flight.

Ellis said not to overthink the choice. If it's still unclear what is in flight, ask once. Related: [[hackathon-speed]], [[ticket-updates]].

=== ios-simulator-on-ellis-mac.md
---
name: ios-simulator-on-ellis-mac
description: "On Ellis's Mac (Xcode 27, DeviceHub, no Simulator.app) Ellis starts simulators; agents only install and launch into the booted one"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 829c4789-d388-4f09-ab14-3b824c7938d2
  modified: 2026-11-14T23:33:11.996Z
---

On 2026-11-14 I booted an iPhone simulator with `xcrun simctl boot` for Kip. Ellis then could not press Start in DeviceHub ("Unable to boot device in current state: Booted", code 405) and asked me to stop booting it: "ur booting it and not letting me click start".

**Why:** Xcode 27 has no Simulator.app; DeviceHub is the simulator UI and only shows devices it started itself. `xcode-select` on this Mac points at the Command Line Tools, so Xcode tools need `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`. Force-killing CoreSimulatorService left CoreDeviceService (a user process) holding a stale connection, so DeviceHub's Start silently did nothing until CoreDeviceService was restarted.

**How to apply:**
- Never `simctl boot` or `open devices://...`; ask Ellis to start a device in DeviceHub, then wait for it to show as Booted.
- Build with `xcodebuild ... -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator'` (or `expo run:ios --no-bundler`), then `xcrun simctl install` + `launch` into the booted UDID, and screenshot with `xcrun simctl io <udid> screenshot`.
- Never kill CoreSimulatorService. If Start does nothing, check `/usr/bin/log show` (zsh's `log` builtin shadows it) for boot actions stuck in CoreDeviceService.
Related: [[hackathon-speed]].
=== merges-outside-hq-ship.md
---
name: merges-outside-hq-ship
description: "Ellis sometimes merges PRs from GitHub/Conductor instead of ./hq ship, which skips unblocking dependent issues"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5956363b-d67f-42fa-9375-f7295fff282a
  modified: 2026-11-14T18:59:10.130Z
---

On 2026-11-14 Ellis merged PR #134 (#52) directly, not through `./hq ship`, so the ship step that flips dependents from `status:blocked` to `status:ready` and comments "Unblocked: #N merged in #PR" never ran. #53 stayed blocked until I ran that step by hand.

**Why:** `./hq ship` is the only thing that unblocks dependents. A UI merge closes the issue (via `Closes #N`) and Entire marks the trail complete, but labels on other issues don't change.

**How to apply:** when a PR of mine turns out merged, or Ellis asks whether issues are updated, check open `status:blocked` issues whose "Blocked by" refs are now all closed. Use hq's own `unblock_candidates` logic for the check, then apply the same label flip and comment. Closed issues keep their last status label; that's normal in this repo, and there is no "done" label. Related: [[check-in-flight-work-before-claiming]], [[hackathon-speed]].
=== ticket-updates.md
---
name: ticket-updates
description: Always keep the tickets I (or agents I dispatch) work on current on GitHub; reviewing tickets is read-only unless Ellis asks for edits
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4a9f6dc5-fe85-47ec-abde-6f9d440d834b
  modified: 2026-11-14T19:19:33.389Z
---

Ellis wants every issue I or my dispatched agents work on kept up to date on GitHub, every time:
- claim: `status:in-progress`;
- PR open: `status:review`;
- acceptance-criteria boxes ticked once each one is verified, with a short evidence comment;
- follow-ups linked in a comment;
- on merge: closed, boxes ticked, stale status label removed, and dependents unblocked the way `./hq ship` does.

"Go through the tickets" means read and evaluate them, not edit them. On 2026-11-14 I started relabelling other people's issues during a review pass, and Ellis stopped me: "I didn't ask you to bring any tickets' reality up to date".

**Why:** the board is the team's shared state. My own issues must be accurate; other people's tickets are theirs to change.

**How to apply:** update tickets for issues I claim or dispatch, and put the same rule in every agent brief. For anything else, report what looks stale and ask before editing. Related: [[check-in-flight-work-before-claiming]].

result.output:
# Spec

What we build. `/hq-plan` turns it into issues. Business detail is in `docs/BUSINESS.md`, the
science and wording rules in `docs/DOMAIN.md`.

## Problem
The city measures night noise, but people feel it, and nobody connects the two. Newcastle's
Urban Observatory publishes kerbside noise levels and WHO publishes how night noise disturbs sleep,
yet a resident can't tell what woke them, and a traveller can't tell that a hotel overlooks a
24-hour demolition site. Bewick Court residents were kept awake until 5am by demolition under a
24-hour permit, and no open dataset recorded it.

## Product
Kip shows how the city's noise affects sleep, street by street, and turns that into a Quiet Stay
Score for every hotel in Newcastle. It has three layers:

| Layer | Feature | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| City | City sleep map | Each Observatory noise sensor shaded by an indicative % of nearby residents highly sleep disturbed |
| Personal | Personal night | Timeline of sleep stages, bedroom noise and wake-ups, each tagged with its likely cause |
| Personal | Morning briefing | Spoken summary on Watch or AirPods: "Two wake-ups followed drilling at 06:41, before the 8am limit" |
| Personal | Evidence log | An out-of-hours noise report for the council, its hash anchored on Solana |
| Business | Quiet Stays | Hotels ranked by predicted sleep quality for the traveller's profile, with booking links |

City map and Personal night are the core; the rest build on them.

## Users
- **Resident** near construction or nightlife: wants to know what wakes them and whether it broke
  the council's construction hours, with evidence they can send.
- **Traveller** choosing a Newcastle hotel: wants to know where they will sleep well, weighted for
  how they travel (light sleeper, night out, best value, business).
- **Judges**: see real city data, a real recorded night and one live noise event.

## Demo script (3 min)
One live moment carries the pitch: a drilling sound hits the phone, and Kip labels it, checks the
council's hours and briefs you within seconds.

| # | Time | Step | P |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0:00 | Hook: Bewick Court. "Where in Newcastle would you sleep worst tonight? Nobody can tell you. Kip can." | P0 |
| 2 | 0:20 | City map: real Observatory data, sensors shaded by an indicative 30-night estimate of residents highly sleep disturbed | P0 |
| 3 | 0:50 | Live noise event: phone on the table in demo mode (no Watch data). ElevenLabs-generated drilling clip played from a speaker held against it. Dashboard shows the spike, Gemini labels it "construction", Kip flags it as outside council hours, the ElevenLabs briefing plays | P0 |
| 4 | 1:40 | A real night recorded at home: sleep stages, bedroom noise, wake-ups, shown as counts against the random baseline | P0 |
| 5 | 2:10 | Quiet Stays: switch profile "Light sleeper" to "Night out", ranking reorders; a hotel penalised for works on the stay dates | P0 |
| 6 | 2:35 | Trust: edit a log, show it no longer matches its Solana memo. Flash `terraform plan` and the Entire session record | P1 |
| 7 | 2:50 | Business: affiliate commission now, Verified Quiet next, data licensing later | P0 (slide) |

If a P1 step isn't working at the freeze, cut it from the script rather than slip.

## MVP scope (M1)
- Kip app on iOS (Expo): relative dB logged once a second, a 10-second clip around each spike,
  on-device check that drops clips with speech, recording while locked, HealthKit read of the
  Watch's sleep stages, heart rate, HRV and respiratory rate after the night ends, upload to the
  API, and a live demo mode that streams dB.
- Ingest worker: Observatory noise, NO2 and PM2.5 every 5 minutes, plus a backfill of at least
  30 nights; OpenStreetMap hotels and venues.
- API: night upload, clip labelling (Gemini, then delete the clip), wake-up attribution,
  construction-hours check, briefing text (Gemini) and voice (ElevenLabs), city map data, hotel
  ranking per profile, Street Manager SNS endpoint (or a recorded sample).
- Kip app on web (same Expo codebase, the demo dashboard): city map, night timeline, live event
  view, Quiet Stays page.
- Deployed on Vultr via Terraform, HTTPS via Caddy on an sslip.io hostname.

## Non-goals
- Calibrated dB from the phone. Kip uses spikes relative to the night's own baseline.
- Room-level hotel scores. The score describes a hotel's surroundings.
- Claiming noise *caused* a wake-up. Kip shows a link.
- Real affiliate bookings. Demo links are placeholders.
- Building or demolition sites outside Street Manager, except as heard by the bedroom microphone.
- An all-night Watch workout session (drains 40% to 100% of the battery). Read HealthKit instead.

## Stretch (M2, in priority order)
1. Solana Memo anchoring and the tamper demo (P1).
2. ElevenLabs Scribe as a second noise classifier; disagreements become "uncertain" (P1).
3. Complaint draft for the council from the evidence log (P1).
4. Simulated user cohort on the map and in hotel scores, labelled as simulated (P1).
5. Native watchOS target: haptics, "something woke me" button, briefing playback. Only if Watch signing
   works in the first 2 hours (P2).
6. Air quality factor in the hotel score (P2).

## Open questions
These change the plan. All are answered.
- Does one of us sleep at home in Newcastle during the event, near an Observatory noise sensor?
  ANSWERED (2026-11-14): No. The city map uses sensors near the venue, and demo step 4 uses a night
  exported from HealthKit.
- How long is the event, and when does it start? ANSWERED (2026-11-14): 24 hours, from Sat 14 Nov 2026
  12:00 to Sun 15 Nov 2026 12:00, which is also the code freeze.
- Is each team limited to one sponsor track? ANSWERED (2026-11-14): Yes. Enter MongoDB: see
  `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

# Kip app

One Expo app builds the iPhone app and the web dashboard (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`). Expo Go cannot
run it: HealthKit, background audio and the Mapbox SDK need a dev client build.

## Run on the iOS simulator

Needs Xcode with an iOS simulator runtime, and CocoaPods (`brew install cocoapods`).

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` at the repo root and fill in `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_MOBILE_TOKEN`
   (see Mapbox below). The app stops at launch without `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`, and without the token
   the map shows a message instead of Newcastle. A teammate can pull the token from the repo's
   Actions variables: `gh variable get EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_MOBILE_TOKEN`.
2. If `xcode-select -p` prints `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools`, point the build at Xcode:
   `export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`.
3. Start a simulator. On Xcode 27 it lives in DeviceHub, not Simulator.app.
4. Build and install the dev client. `apps/mobile/ios/` is generated and gitignored.

   ```sh
   bun install
   cd apps/mobile && bunx expo run:ios --no-bundler
   ```

5. Start Metro from the repo root so it reads `.env`, then open the server in the dev client:

   ```sh
   bun run dev:app
   ```

Repeat step 4 only after changing `app.config.ts` or a native package. For JS or `.env` changes,
restart Metro (step 5) and reload.

## Mapbox

The iPhone map uses `@rnmapbox/maps` (Mapbox Maps SDK for iOS) behind `src/lib/map`. It draws the
same `light-v11` style and overlay layers as the web map.

- **Runtime token:** create a public `pk.` token in your Mapbox account with the default public
  scopes and no URL restriction. Store it as `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_MOBILE_TOKEN` in `.env`. Keep it
  separate from the web token (`EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN`), so the web token's URL restrictions
  never block the phone.
- **Build credentials: none.** CocoaPods downloads the SDK without a token.
  `$RNMapboxMapsDownloadToken` is deprecated in `@rnmapbox/maps` 10.3. Do not create a secret
  `sk.` download token for this build. If a later SDK version needs one again, keep it in
  `~/.netrc` on the build Mac. Never commit it or put it in an `EXPO_PUBLIC_` variable, because
  those ship inside the app. The app refuses an `sk.` token.
- **Location:** browsing the map asks for no location permission. The map shows no user-location
  puck.
- **Attribution:** the Mapbox logo and the attribution button stay on.

## Run on a physical iPhone

HealthKit and background audio only work on a real iPhone, not in Expo Go or the simulator.

Needs a Mac with Xcode, an Apple ID signed in under Xcode, and the iPhone on USB with Developer Mode
on (Settings, Privacy & Security). Use Xcode 27.2 or later (`/Applications/Xcode.app`): the Xcode 27.0
beta lacks the iOS 27 header API that `react-native-screens` needs and fails to compile.

1. Follow steps 1 and 2 above (`.env` at the repo root, `DEVELOPER_DIR` pointing at Xcode).
2. Build and install: `cd apps/mobile && bunx expo run:ios --device --no-bundler`, then pick the iPhone.
3. First run: in Xcode, open `apps/mobile/ios/*.xcworkspace`, select the Kip target, Signing &
   Capabilities, choose your team and change `com.durhack.kip` if Apple rejects it. HealthKit must
   appear under capabilities.
4. On the phone: Settings, General, VPN & Device Management, trust your developer certificate.
5. Start Metro from the repo root (`bun run dev:app`) and open it in the dev client.

`EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values are inlined when Metro bundles, so a Metro started without
`EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` makes the app stop at launch. Set it in `.env` and restart Metro with
`--clear`. The live API is `https://kip.edenmatrix.xyz`. It is public and ends up in the bundle:
never put a secret in an `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` variable.

## What the config sets (`app.config.ts`)

- HealthKit: `@kingstinct/react-native-healthkit` adds the `com.apple.developer.healthkit`
  entitlement and `NSHealthShareUsageDescription`. Kip only reads, so `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`

- [ ] With the phone locked, audio metering keeps running
- [ ] The app reaches `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL`

# Domain

The science, rules and wording Kip depends on. Code that computes, labels or displays any of
these must follow this file. Constants live in `packages/shared/src/domain/`, not inline.

## Night noise and the WHO curve
- **Night window:** 23:00 to 07:00, `Europe/London` local time (handle BST changes).
- **Lnight:** the A-weighted equivalent level over the night window. It is an *energy* average,
  not an arithmetic mean of dB:
  `Lnight = 10 * log10(mean(10 ^ (L_i / 10)))`.
  In Tiger, average `power(10, db / 10)` and convert back with `10 * log10(...)`.
- **City estimate:** per sensor, the energy average of nightly Lnight over at least the last 30
  nights. Fewer than 30 nights: show the sensor as "not enough data", don't shade it.
- **WHO road-traffic curve** (Basner & McGuire 2018), % highly sleep disturbed:
  `%HSD = 19.4312 - 0.9336 * Lnight + 0.0126 * Lnight^2`.
  This reproduces the plan's figures (2.9% at 45 dB, 6.2% at 55 dB, 8.8% at 60 dB). Still check
  the paper before quoting more decimals.
- **Valid range:** 40 to 65 dB Lnight. Outside it, clamp for shading and mark the value as
  out of range; never extrapolate.
- **Thresholds** (WHO 2018): night-time road traffic below 45 dB Lnight, rail 44 dB, aircraft
  40 dB.
- **Limits:** the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise at a home's most exposed facade.
  Observatory sensors sit at the kerb and also pick up nightlife and voices. So the map is an
  *indicative road-traffic estimate*, never a measured disturbance rate.

## Bedroom noise (phone)
- The iPhone microphone is not calibrated. Store and show **relative dB** only.
- Sample once a second. A **spike** is a level above the night's own baseline (rolling median)
  by a threshold set in `packages/shared`. Keep a 10-second clip around each spike.
- On-device voice-activity check: any clip containing speech is dropped on the phone and never
  uploaded.

## Wake-up attribution
- **Wake-up signals:** a Watch "awake" stage during the sleep session, or a sudden heart-rate
  jump during sleep (Watch stages are coarse and miss brief arousals).
- **Method:** look for a spike in the 60 to 120 seconds before each wake-up, and compare the hit
  rate against randomly chosen windows of the same length from the same night.
- **Small numbers:** one night has 2 to 6 wake-ups. Show counts ("3 of 4 wake-ups followed a
  spike"). Show a percentage only once several nights are pooled from HealthKit history.
- HealthKit sleep stages appear only after the sleep session ends. Live demo mode needs no Watch
  data.

## Noise classification
- Labels: `construction`, `traffic`, `siren`, `snoring`, `other`, plus `uncertain` and `handling`.
- **Handling noise** is the phone itself: rubbing on a sleeve, a pocket, a pillow or bedsheets.
  Kip's own small model (trained by us, see `ml/`) runs on each spike clip before Gemini. A clip
  that is mostly handling noise is labelled `handling`; otherwise the model's cleaned audio goes on
  to labelling. `handling` events are never linked to wake-ups and never appear in a briefing.
- Clips travel as 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, so the server needs no audio decoder.
- Gemini (paid-tier key) labels each clip, with JSON output. ElevenLabs Scribe audio-event tags
  give a second opinion. Where they disagree, the event is `uncertain`. This stops a user's own
  snoring being blamed on the building site.
- The clip is deleted once labelled. Only the label is kept.

## Construction hours (Newcastle City Council)
Recommended hours for noisy construction work:

| Day | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Monday to Friday | 08:00 to 18:00 |
| Saturday | 08:00 to 13:00 |
| Sunday and bank holidays | None |

A `construction` event outside these hours is flagged "outside council hours". Bank holidays for
England come from `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` (`england-and-wales`). These are
*recommended* hours: say "outside the council's recommended hours", not "illegal".

## Street Manager
DfT Street Manager pushes street and road works permits in England (location, work category,
traffic management type, proposed and actual times) over AWS SNS to a public HTTPS endpoint. The
subscription must be confirmed within 3 days. It covers roads, not building or demolition sites.
Night work is inferred from proposed times and traffic management type.

## Evidence log and Solana
Each night's log is serialised canonically, hashed (SHA-256), and the hash written to Solana
mainnet with the Memo program (no Anchor). It proves *when* a log existed, not that its contents
are true. Never claim more.

## Wording rules
Anything user-facing, in the briefing prompt, the app (iOS or web) or the pitch:

export { NightTimelineChart, type NightTimelineSlots } from "./components";
export { NightScreen } from "./screens/NightScreen";
import type { NightTimeline } from "@kip/shared/night";
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useTRPC } from "@/lib/trpc";
import { Button, Card, Screen, Text } from "@/lib/ui";
import { NightTimelineChart } from "../components";
import { fixtureNight } from "../data/fixture";

type State =
  | { kind: "loading" }
  | { kind: "error"; retry: () => void }
  | { kind: "night"; night: NightTimeline; simulated: boolean };

const isStub = (e: unknown) =>
  (e as { data?: { code?: string } } | null)?.data?.code === "NOT_IMPLEMENTED";

/** Latest night from `night.list` then `night.get`. A NOT_IMPLEMENTED backend shows the simulated fixture. */
function useNight(): State {
  const trpc = useTRPC();
  const list = useQuery({ ...trpc.night.list.queryOptions(), retry: false });
  const nights = list.data as { nightId: string; startedAt: string }[] | undefined;
  const latest = nights?.slice().sort((a, b) => b.startedAt.localeCompare(a.startedAt))[0]?.nightId;
  const get = useQuery({
    ...trpc.night.get.queryOptions({ nightId: latest ?? fixtureNight.nightId }),
    enabled: latest !== undefined,
    retry: false,
  });
  if (list.isPending || (latest !== undefined && get.isPending)) return { kind: "loading" };
  const live = get.data as NightTimeline | undefined;
  if (live) return { kind: "night", night: live, simulated: false };
  if (list.isError && !isStub(list.error)) {
    return { kind: "error", retry: () => void list.refetch() };
  }
  if (get.isError && !isStub(get.error)) {
    return { kind: "error", retry: () => void get.refetch() };
  }
  return { kind: "night", night: fixtureNight, simulated: true };
}

export function NightScreen() {
  const state = useNight();
  return (
    <Screen>
      <Text variant="title">Your night</Text>
      {state.kind === "loading" && <Text variant="caption">Loading your night.</Text>}
      {state.kind === "error" && (
        <Card>
          <Text>We could not load your night.</Text>
          <Button label="Try again" onPress={state.retry} />
        </Card>
      )}
      {state.kind === "night" && (
        <>
          <Text variant="caption">
            {state.night.night}. Noise is in relative dB from the phone microphone, not calibrated.
            {state.simulated ? " Simulated night." : ""}
          </Text>
          <Card>
            <NightTimelineChart night={state.night} />
          </Card>
        </>
      )}
    </Screen>
  );
}

# hq-work

`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.

1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).

PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:

````markdown
## What changed
- <what the product can now do>

## How verified
- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
```
<tail of ./hq check>
```

## Risks
- <what could break, or "none">

## Screenshots
<UI changes only, else "n/a">
````

Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.

Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.

Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).

Read this before drafting. The failure mode is drifting into an engineering
narrative, and it is easy to do without noticing.

## The flow: draft, confirm, commit, they push

1. **Draft** the message and show it in one plain code block.
2. **Wait.** Never commit on the same turn as the draft. The user is reviewing both
   the message and the commit boundary.
3. **On confirmation**, write the body to `.context/commit-message.txt` (gitignored),
   `git add` only that stage's files, then
   `git commit -F .context/commit-message.txt`.
4. **Stop.** Never `git push`. The user pushes once they agree with what landed.

### Authorship, non-negotiable

The commit is the user's. Their git config supplies the author. Never pass `--author`,
never add `Co-Authored-By`, never add any AI attribution or trailer line of any kind.

### Before committing, mechanically check

    python3 -c "import sys;b=open('.context/commit-message.txt',encoding='utf-8').read();\
    bad=[c for c in b if c in '\u2014\u2013'];print('DASHES:',bad or 'none')"

Any hit, rewrite it. Colons, commas or hyphens instead. Also confirm no `Co-Authored-By`,
no full file paths, and no test counts in the body.

### Scope

One stage per commit. Add that stage's files by name rather than `git add -A`, unless the
user says otherwise. If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## Shape

```
<Imperative subject: what the product or system gained>

<Paragraph: what exists now, and honestly what it still does not do.>

<Optional second paragraph: the one decision worth defending, and why.>

- Filename.php: what changed here and why.
- area or filename: what changed here and why.
- tests: what is covered, and how the assertions were proven to have teeth.
```

## The subject line

Imperative, no full stop, names what was added or changed at product level.

Good, taken from real commits in this style:

```
Add the relational policy schema, models and the attention rule
Import legacy governance into relational policies and add the library index
Gate every governance write on canEditWorkspace
Scope policies to the property group
Align policies-v2 docs to company ownership
```

If the subject needs "and also", it should have been two commits.

## The opening paragraph: be additive

This is the part that goes wrong. Lead with **what the system can now do**, and
state plainly what it still cannot. Two real examples:

> First structural phase of the Policies rebuild: the tables exist and are
> unit-testable, and nothing reads them yet, so the change is additive and
> invisible.

> The importer builds each workspace from the real taxonomy and only overlays
> whatever was saved before, because the old data can't be trusted.

Both open with the thing that now exists. Neither opens with the process of
building it.

## Bullets

One per file or area. **Bare filenames or short area names, never full paths.**
Dense prose sentences, not fragments. Reasoning inline, in the same sentence as
the change.

```
- PolicyEventTypeEnum.php: fourteen cases, the single vocabulary behind history
  chips, the Agent Log filter options and the WorkOS action names. Values stay
  inside string(32) so the column does not need widening.
- migrations: policy_events gains uuid, correlation_id and mirrored_at. uuid is
  the event's public identity and the WorkOS idempotency key, so a retried mirror
  cannot duplicate upstream.
```

Group related files under one area bullet (`migrations:`, `tests:`) rather than
listing each.

The last bullet is always `tests:`, covering what is asserted and, where
mutation testing was done, that the assertions fail without the fix.

## Plain words, and few of them

Write for someone skimming `git log`, not for someone admiring the design.

**Cut invented precision.** Phrases that sound exact but carry no meaning to a
reader: "taxonomy positions", "the canonical vocabulary", "the seam", "first-class
records", "the discipline". If a plainer sentence says the same thing, use it.

    no    References are taxonomy positions, not free text
    yes   A new policy is numbered automatically from its category

    no    the write path funnels through a single mutation surface
    yes   all edits go through PolicyWriteService

**Keep bullets to one or two sentences.** If a bullet needs three, either the
change is doing too much or the detail belongs in the code comment instead.

**Say the effect, not the mechanism**, unless the mechanism is the point.

    no    ds-form-control applies text-transform uppercase and the console body
          carries the hq-app class so the cascade reaches it
    yes   dialog fields show what was typed. They were inheriting the HQ form
          style, which forces uppercase.

**Target length.** Subject, a short paragraph, one optional second paragraph, then
one bullet per file. If it runs much past that, cut rather than reorganise.

## Do not

- **Tell the story of finding the bug.** "Two faults surfaced only by driving it",
  "a test caught", "it turned out", "I discovered". The reader wants the state of
  the system, not the diary. If a fault is worth mentioning, say what the code now
  does and why, in one clause.
- **Lead with process.** Not "after the merge I ran the suite and". Lead with the change.
- **Headline test counts.** "195 tests passing" belongs in chat, not the message.
  Numbers that age badly do not belong in permanent history.
- **Use full file paths.** `PolicyWriteService.php`, not
  `app/Services/Policies/PolicyWriteService.php`.
- **Use em-dashes anywhere.** Colons, commas or hyphens instead. This applies to
  every generated artifact, not just commits.
- **Narrate the plan.** No stage numbers, phase names, ticket references or
  "as agreed". The commit records the code, not the schedule.

## Self-check before handing it over

1. Does the first sentence say what the system can now do?
2. Could a reader who was not in the conversation follow it?
3. Is every bullet a change plus its reason, rather than a list of edits?
4. Any discovery narrative left? Cut it.
5. Any em-dash? Any full path? Any test count in the body? Cut them.
6. Would the subject still make sense in a changelog?
House style applies, but per CLAUDE.md I commit and push on my own branch without waiting for approval, and AGENTS.md rules out co-author trailers.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ellishewes/conductor/workspaces/durhack-proj/porto-novo/.claude/skills/anti-slop

If `.ux-profile.md` exists at the project root, read it before changing layout, color, or type.

### Intent

AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.

### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)

- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.

### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles

- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.
- If it appears in a generic SaaS landing template, assume it is slop until proven functional.
- Cross-check `.ux-profile.md` banned list — it may extend these rules.

### Concrete Scenarios (Before vs. After)

#### ❌ Anti-Pattern

Sign-up uses a `conic-gradient` "Get Started" button. Login form inputs each have a leading gray icon. Empty project view shows a cartoon character high-fiving. Settings show "Last updated" inside a lavender pill. A modal uses `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` with no border on a busy background.

#### ✅ Best Practice

Primary CTA is solid accent fill. Search field keeps one magnifier icon; other fields are label + input only. Empty state: heading, one sentence of value, "Create project" button, optional simple 24px monochrome icon. Metadata runs as 12px secondary text. Modal uses opaque L3 surface, 1px border, optional scrim — no blur.

### Framework-Agnostic Implementation Blueprint

**Audit pass (grep / search changed files):**

```
backdrop-filter
conic-gradient
linear-gradient.*(#.*,#.*,#)   /* multi-hue gradients on buttons */
illustration|empty-state.*svg  /* review for cartoon people */
border-radius: 999             /* pill wrappers on static text */
```

**Replace patterns:**

```css
/* ❌ Slop */
.btn-primary {
  background: conic-gradient(from 180deg, #f00, #ff0, #0f0, #00f, #f0f);
}
.panel {
  backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
}

/* ✅ Restrained */
.btn-primary {
  background: var(--accent);
}
.panel {
  background: var(--surface-l3);
  border: 1px solid var(--border-l2);
}
```

Use [reference/slop-checklist.md](reference/slop-checklist.md) for the full identification matrix.

### Agent Checklist

- [ ] Read `.ux-profile.md` if present; merge its ban list with this skill.
- [ ] Scan CTAs — no rainbow or multi-hue radial gradients.
- [ ] Scan overlays — no unbounded glassmorphism; border + opaque fallback if blur exists.
- [ ] Scan empty states — no cartoon people illustrations.
- [ ] Scan inputs — icons only where functional (search, clear, toggle).
- [ ] Scan metadata — no decorative pill wrappers on static text.
- [ ] After a slop pass: list frame, row dividers, and search chrome still present — an empty-looking table is a fail.
- [ ] Run slop checklist matrix on any AI-generated or imported component.

## What changed
- The phone now reads what the Apple Watch tracked overnight from HealthKit: sleep stages (inBed, awake, core, deep, rem), heart rate, HRV (SDNN) and breathing rate, shaped as `NightUpload.sleep`. `watchSleep` reads a recording's window (`readWindow`), one past night (`readNight`), or several past nights in one HealthKit query for pooling (`readPastNights`).

- The Watch wins. When it recorded the night, the iPhone's in-bed time and other sleep apps are dropped, so two sources never share one timeline. "In bed" only fills gaps between stages, stages never overlap, vitals are `[epoch seconds, value]`, and every datetime carries its Europe/London offset.
- The Night tab shows a "Last night from your Apple Watch" card: the stages on the timeline's own band, time asleep and in each stage, wake-ups, heart-rate range, HRV and breathing rate. It renders nothing on the web.

## For the reviewer
- **File name:** the iOS file is `native/healthkit.native.ts`, not `.ios.ts`. The app's tsconfig resolves platform files through `moduleSuffixes: [".native", ""]`, as `lib/map/Map.native.tsx` does, so TypeScript checks callers against the real implementation. Metro picks it on iOS and `healthkit.web.ts` on the web.

- **Unspecified sleep:** HealthKit's "asleep, unspecified" (watchOS 8 and older, some apps) maps to `core`, the closest stage `NightUpload` has.
- **Past nights** are read from 18:00 to 12:00 London time, wider than the 23:00 to 07:00 Lnight window, so a whole sleep session fits. A recording's own start and stop can be passed instead.

# claude-code review

Verdict: request changes. The card and `NightUpload.sleep` take in every Watch vital from 18:00 to 12:00, waking hours included. That skews the "Asleep" span, the stage band's scale and the heart-rate range. I found 8 issues and did not run the tests.

- [medium] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:203` `vitalsIn` keeps every heart rate, HRV and breathing sample whose start falls anywhere in `nightWindow` (18:00 to 12:00). The Watch records heart rate all day, so a night with stages from 23:30 to 07:00 also uploads roughly 5.5 waking hours of evening readings and 5 hours of morning ones as `sleep.heartRate`. An evening workout gives a row like "Heart rate 52 to 165 bpm", and the server's heart-rate wake-up detection reads waking data as sleep data. Fix: when there are stages, clip the vitals to the first and last stage, and

- [medium] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:243` `startedAt`/`endedAt` are the earliest and latest moments across both stages and vitals. With all-day heart rate they come out near 18:00 and 12:00. So `watch-copy.ts:49` shows "Asleep 7 h, 18:01 to 11:58", and `WatchNightCard.tsx:65` scales the stage band over 18 hours, which squeezes the real stages into the middle of the bar. Fix: take the span from the stage segments when there are any, and fall back to the vitals only for a night with no stages.

- [medium] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:104` `lastNight` uses `nightOf(now - 12h)`, so it moves to the next night at London midnight rather than after the night ends. At 00:30 on Nov 16 "last night" becomes Nov 15, the night now in progress. Evening heart-rate readings already exist, so the card says "Last night from your Apple Watch" with "Recorded 18:02 to 00:29, no sleep stages" (or "no data") until noon the next day. Fix: switch at the window's end (12:00) or at sleep end, for example `nightOf(now) === today ? yesterday : ...`, or keep the previous night until `nig

- [medium] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:130` `preferWatch` keeps every sample with `fromWatch` true, whatever its source. A third-party sleep app on the Watch (AutoSleep, Pillow) also writes samples with a `Watch…` product type, so its stages mix with Apple's. `trimOverlaps` then builds a band that switches between the two apps' guesses, which breaks the "two apps never interleave" promise. Fix: inside the Watch samples, also pick one `sourceId`, preferring `com.apple.health.*` or the source with the most samples.

- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:49` `asleepUnspecified` is mapped to `"core"`. A night without stages (watchOS 8 and older, iPhone-only or third-party sources) then shows as "Core 7 h" on the card and uploads as core stages. That is a stage the device never measured, and it gets counted in the per-stage analysis. Fix: label unspecified sleep as plain asleep, which means a separate stage value through a contract issue. Short of that, don't list a "Core" row when every segment came from value 1.

- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/screens/NightScreen.tsx:63` `<WatchNightCard />` always shows HealthKit's "last night" under a timeline that may be another night: the latest server night, or the simulated fixture. The screen can show "2026-11-10 … Simulated night." above "Last night from your Apple Watch", with nothing saying they are different nights. Fix: read the Watch night that matches `state.night.night`, or name the card's night date.

- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:337` `readPastNights` makes one HealthKit read from `nightWindow(oldest).start` to `nightWindow(latest).end` with `limit: 0` on all four types. For 30 nights that pulls every heart-rate sample from about 30 days, including dense workout sampling and the 12:00 to 18:00 gaps that get thrown away. That is tens of thousands of objects in JS memory on the phone. Fix: read each `nightWindow` on its own (in parallel), or pass an OR of the night windows as the date filter.

- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/hooks/useWatchNight.ts:23` Only the pure reader and the copy are tested. Nothing tests that `useWatchNight` stays at "loading" without reading while consent is loading, or that turning health consent off switches the card to `no-consent` through the `queryKey`. That consent gating is the issue's privacy requirement. Fix: add a hook test with mocked `useConsent` and `watchSleep`.

# claude-code review

Request changes. A stale "no-consent" result can stay cached under the consent-on key, so the Watch card can stay on the consent prompt after the user turns Health back on.

- [medium] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/hooks/useWatchNight.ts:23` The key is `["night", "watch", night, consent.health]`, but `queryFn` reads consent from the account cache. "Delete everything" calls `resetQueries()`, which refetches the mounted query under the `true` key. By then the account cache is empty, so `healthConsentOf(undefined)` gives "no-consent" and that result is stored under the `true` key with `staleTime: 10 * 60_000`. If the user re-onboards with Health on within 10 minutes, the key is `true` again and the cached result counts as fresh. The card keeps showing "Allow Health in the Account tab", and the no-consent state has no retry button. Fix: give non-ok results a stale
- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/hooks/useWatchNight.ts:20` `night = lastNight(new Date())` is only recomputed on render, and the `queryFn` closure keeps that `night`. If the app opens before 06:00 and comes back to the foreground after it, React Query's focus refetch re-reads the old night. When the data is unchanged nothing re-renders, so the card keeps showing the night before last. Fix: recompute `night` on app focus or put it in state with a timer at the next 06:00, or work out the night inside `queryFn` and return it with the data.
- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:255` The session runs from the first to the last stage segment anywhere in the 18:00 to 12:00 window. If the Watch writes a second, earlier sleep session (a nap at 19:00, or a session that started before 18:00 and was clipped to it), every vital from the evening gap counts as "sleep" again. That undoes the "waking hours never count" fix. Fix: split the segments into sessions at large gaps (say over 1 to 2 hours) and keep the longest one, or the one that overlaps `quietWindow`.
- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/healthkit.native.ts:49` `during()` decides between a single `date` filter and `{ OR: dates }`, and is the only code that turns the past-night windows into a HealthKit predicate. It has no test. A wrong shape would either read the afternoons between nights or nothing at all. The native library also logs a warning for an OR with fewer than 2 entries. Fix: export `during` and add a unit test for 1 and for 2 or more windows.
- [low] `apps/mobile/src/features/night/native/watch-sleep.ts:327` The `no-data` doc says it covers "the sleep session has not ended yet". In fact, before the stages arrive, the no-stage fallback returns `ok` with the vitals from 23:00 to 07:00. After 06:00 the card therefore shows "Recorded ..., no sleep stages" as last night, cached for 10 minutes, instead of the no-data hint about stages arriving after you wake. Fix: when a Watch heart-rate series exists but there are no stages and `now` is before the end of the quiet window plus some margin, return no-data. content.text:
The simulated users are now in the production database, and there are two ways to turn them off. None of it shows on the live map until the code is shipped, though.

**What went in.** I added 91 simulated people across 17 Newcastle and Gateshead neighbourhoods, each with 5 nights: 455 nights in total. The simulated-night count went from 0 to 455.
- **Where they live:** neighbourhoods within about 4 km of Grey's Monument, weighted towards student and city-centre areas (Jesmond, Heaton, Sandyford, City Centre, Haymarket, Quayside). Each person has a random home inside their area, and areas by the Tyne are kept small so homes stay on land.
- **How the nights look:** everyone has their own bedtime and wake time, livelier areas are louder with more noise spikes, and no night is stored before it has ended.
- **What it touches:** only nights marked as simulated. Real users' data and "Delete everything" are unaffected.

**One thing I fixed along the way.** Quiet Stays counts nights recorded near each hotel and would have reported the simulated ones as real. It now flags them as simulated. Nothing on screen shows that count yet, but the live API mislabels it until this ships.

**Turning it off**
- **On the map:** a "Show simulated people" switch in the legend. It's on by default and each device remembers its setting, so your demo phone or the projector stays as you set it. With it off, the map shows only areas with 3 or more real people.
- **For everyone:** one command on the server removes them all. Running the seed again brings back the same 91 people. Just ask and I'll run either.

**To make it visible**, say "ship it" in this order:
1. [#187](https://github.com/ehewes/durhack-proj/pull/187), the heat layer on the map.
